Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component (already checked out). Step 1 already committed (ZimmSlideIndicator). Build Step 2 of the SFCC-236 plan ONLY.

## IMPORTANT — naming, read before anything else
The plan originally called these `ZimmSizeSelectorOption`/`ZimmSizeSelector`. **That name is now claimed by unrelated, unmerged work** (`feature/SFCC-92_pdp-size-selection-add-to-bag`, a completely different dropdown-based component for the PDP). To avoid a collision, this step builds:
- **`ZimmSizeChip`** (atom) — was `ZimmSizeSelectorOption`
- **`ZimmSizeChipGroup`** (molecule) — was `ZimmSizeSelector`

Do NOT use "SizeSelector" anywhere — not in a folder name, component name, recipe key, comment, or test description. If you see "SizeSelector" anywhere in what follows, mentally substitute the new names.

## Create ONLY these 8 files
```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/index.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/index.stories.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/index.test.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/zimmSizeChip.css.ts

overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/index.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/index.stories.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/index.test.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts
```
Plus register BOTH new recipes in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — two import lines, two entries in the `components` export object. Do not touch any other line in that file, and do not touch any file outside this list (in particular, do NOT touch anything in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDropdown/` or `hooks/useZimmSizeSelector.ts` if either exists on disk — they belong to unrelated, unmerged work and are not present on this branch anyway).

## Mandatory: read the exemplar pair FIRST, in full
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` (index.tsx, .css.ts, index.stories.tsx, index.test.tsx) and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/` (same four files). This atom/molecule pair is the exact structural mirror of what you're building — colour swatch (atom, one clickable circle) / swatch group (molecule, the row + keyboard nav + roving tabindex), copy its conventions precisely: naming, export style, props placement, recipe key pattern, `useMultiStyleConfig` usage, `__css`/`chakra.*` usage, i18n via `defineMessages`, and the test/story structure. Pay particular attention to `zimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `handleSwatchesKeyDown` function — you are copying its arrow-key/roving-tabindex logic, adapted for a size chip row instead of a colour swatch row.

## Design source (verified Figma structure — do not re-derive, use as given)
- `ZimmSizeChip` (atom) ← Figma `.base-size-selector`, node `40003038:125876`. Component set with **4 states**: `State=Default` (`…125875`) | `State=Selected` (`…125874`) | `State=Focus` (`…130506`) | `State=Disabled` (`…125873`). All variants are 28×28.
- `ZimmSizeChipGroup` (molecule) ← Figma `Size Selector`, node `40003066:34868`. Component set with **2 types**: `Type=Default` (multi-size row, `…34867`, 208×28) | `Type=One Size` (single non-interactive label, `…34866`, 65×28).

## `ZimmSizeChip` (atom) — behaviour and exact pass criteria
- Renders a native `<button role="radio" aria-checked={isSelected}>`. NOT a plain `<div>` with a click handler — must be a real, natively-focusable, natively-operable button.
- Props: `value: string`, `label: string`, `isSelected: boolean`, `isDisabled?: boolean`, `onSelect: (value: string) => void`.
- **Four states, matching the four Figma variants exactly, all visually and programmatically distinguishable:**
  - **Default** — unselected, enabled.
  - **Selected** — `aria-checked="true"`, distinct visual treatment from Default.
  - **Focus** — uses the SAME focus-ring pattern already established in this codebase: `outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)'` + `outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)'` (grep `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `pageButton` part or `zimmNavItem` for the exact existing var names — use the SAME ones, don't invent new focus-ring tokens). Apply via Chakra's `_focusVisible` pseudo-selector in the recipe, not a manually-toggled class.
  - **Disabled** — sets the real native `disabled` attribute (so it's genuinely inert for both mouse and assistive tech, not just visually greyed), distinct visual treatment.
  - **Hover and Active/pressed are explicitly NOT in the Figma variant set for this component.** Do NOT invent `_hover`/`_active` rules. Ship with neither, and add a one-line comment in the recipe file explaining why (no Figma spec for these states), following the exact precedent of `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `pageButton` part (read it — it does the same thing for the same reason, copy that comment's phrasing/spirit).
- Hit area (the clickable button itself) must be ≥ 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8) even though the Figma chip itself is drawn at 28×28 — 28×28 already clears this, just don't shrink it via padding/border-box tricks.
- `onSelect(value)` fires on click when NOT disabled. Must NOT fire when `isDisabled` is true (verify a disabled button genuinely can't be clicked — native `disabled` attribute handles this, but write a test proving `onSelect` was never called).
- Label text (`label`, e.g. "S", "M", "42") is the visible/accessible content of the button.

## `ZimmSizeChipGroup` (molecule) — behaviour and exact pass criteria
- Renders `role="radiogroup"` with an `aria-label` (via `defineMessages`/`useIntl`, matching the exemplar's i18n pattern) describing the group (e.g. "Select a size").
- Props: `values: ZimmSizeChipValue[]` (exported type — sibling files need it, matching the `ZimmColourSwatchValue` precedent), `selectedValue?: string`, `onSelect?: (value: string) => void`. Each `ZimmSizeChipValue` needs at minimum `{value: string; label: string; isDisabled?: boolean}`.
- **"One Size" variant:** when `values` has exactly one entry, do NOT render a `radiogroup` of `ZimmSizeChip` buttons at all — render a single, non-interactive label element instead (no `role="radio"`, no button, no click handler, no `onSelect` call possible). This matches Figma's `Type=One Size` being a fundamentally different, non-interactive component, not just a radiogroup with one item.
- **Keyboard navigation (multi-size case only), copied from `zimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `handleSwatchesKeyDown`:**
  - ArrowRight/ArrowDown moves selection focus to the next chip; ArrowLeft/ArrowUp to the previous.
  - Wraps at both ends (last→first going forward, first→last going backward).
  - **Skips disabled chips** — arrow navigation must land only on enabled chips, never rest focus on or select a disabled one.
  - Roving tabindex: exactly one chip is in the natural Tab order at a time (`tabIndex={0}` on the "current" chip, `tabIndex={-1}` on the rest) — so Tab enters the group ONCE and Tab again leaves it ONCE, not once per chip.
- `onSelect` fires with the chip's `value` both on click AND on arrow-key navigation landing on a new chip (matching how a native radio group behaves — arrow navigation changes selection, it doesn't just move focus). Never fires for a disabled chip under any input method.
- Composes `ZimmSizeChip` atoms — do not reimplement the button/state logic inline in the group; the group's job is layout + keyboard orchestration only, delegating per-chip rendering to the atom.

## Recipe files
Two separate `.css.ts` files, one per component, following the exact `parts`/`baseStyle` pattern from `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` / `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`:
- `zimmSizeChip.css.ts` exports `export const ZimmSizeChip = {parts: [...], baseStyle: (props) => ({...})}`.
- `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts` exports `export const ZimmSizeChipGroup = {parts: [...], baseStyle: (props) => ({...})}`.
- Recipe keys are the literal strings `'ZimmSizeChip'` and `'ZimmSizeChipGroup'` — do NOT use `'ZimmSizeSelector'` anywhere, and do not collide with any base SFCC recipe name (there is none for either of these names — you're safe, but the point stands for the guard test).
- All colour/spacing as `var(--zimm-*)` — no bare Chakra token keys anywhere (the `recipeGuards.test.ts` hard gate will fail your test run otherwise).
- `parts` array in each file must exactly equal the `styles.X` reads in that component's own `index.tsx` (`recipeParts.test.ts` enforces this per-file).
- No raw hex/px/rem/em literals anywhere except a commented, `provisional`-tagged exception if you genuinely cannot find a matching existing `--zimm-*` token for something Figma specifies (check `overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts`, `sizes.ts`, `colour.ts` first — most things you need almost certainly already have a token, since 28×28/24×24 sizing and radio-style selected/disabled treatments are already established patterns in this codebase via `zimmColourSwatch`).

## Stories
- `ZimmSizeChip`: `title: 'Commerce/ZimmSizeChip'` (this is PDP/card-context, not a generic Elements building block — same categorisation logic as the rest of this build). Mandatory `Default` export, plus named exports for `Selected`, `Disabled`, and a `play`-driven `Focus` demonstration if that's how the exemplar shows focus state (check how `zimmColourSwatch`'s story handles its Focus-equivalent state, if it has one, and mirror that approach).
- `ZimmSizeChipGroup`: `title: 'Commerce/ZimmSizeChipGroup'`. Mandatory `Default` export (multi-size, nothing selected), plus named exports for `WithSelection`, `WithDisabledSize`, `OneSize` (the non-interactive single-label case), and a `play` function demonstrating arrow-key navigation (click to focus first chip, press ArrowRight, assert focus/selection moved) — interactive behaviour worth asserting per this repo's Storybook conventions.

## Tests
Both components need Vitest + RTL coverage matching every pass criterion listed above. Specifically for the group:
- All four arrow keys, including wrap-around at both ends.
- Disabled chips are skipped by arrow navigation (this is the trickiest case — write a specific test with a disabled chip in the middle of the list and confirm ArrowRight jumps over it).
- Tab enters the radiogroup exactly once (assert only one chip has `tabIndex={0}` at any given time, and it updates as arrow-selection changes).
- `onSelect` is called with the right value for both click and arrow-navigation paths, and is never called when the target is disabled.
- The One Size case renders no button, no radiogroup role, and calling nothing happens if some test clicks around it.
- Mock `useMultiStyleConfig` to a flat parts object per the exemplar's pattern. Wrap in `IntlProvider` (`useIntl` throws without one).

## House rules
TypeScript only. Australian spelling in any new prose/comments you write. No `any` without a comment. No non-null assertion without a comment. No hardcoded design-value literal outside `var(--zimm-*)`. No `console.log`. Do not modify `package.json`.

## When done
Report the exact file list created/modified with line counts, confirm nothing outside this list was touched (in particular confirm you did NOT create or touch anything named "SizeSelector"), and confirm all these commands are clean before you report:
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```
Do NOT stage or commit anything.

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { SWATCHES_PER_PAGE } from './zimmColourSwatchGroupShared';
3	
4	/**
5	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is
6	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe
7	 * only lays the group out; each swatch's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the sibling
8	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.
9	 *
10	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for this exact component, not estimated — node
11	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
12	 *
13	 * Six parts:
14	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
15	 *     Capped to a fixed `maxWidth` (`GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH`, see below) unconditionally — not just
16	 *     when paginated — so `labelName`'s truncation CSS always has a definite width to truncate
17	 *     against. See this part's own baseStyle comment for the full explanation.
18	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
19	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
20	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
21	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
22	 *     absolute-position hack.
23	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
24	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
25	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
26	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
27	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children. Once paginated
28	 *     (`isPaginated`), reserves a fixed page-width footprint regardless of how many items the
29	 *     current window actually renders — see its own baseStyle comment below for the layout bug
30	 *     this prevents.
31	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
32	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
33	 */
34	
35	/**
36	 * Imported from the shared zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts module — the same shared-module
37	 * precedent theme/components/footerShared.ts already sets — rather than retyped here, so
38	 * index.tsx, this recipe, and the test file can never disagree with each other. Aliased to the
39	 * shorter `PAGE_SIZE` name since this file's only use is the `GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH` calc
40	 * expression below.
41	 */
42	const PAGE_SIZE = SWATCHES_PER_PAGE;
43	
44	/**
45	 * The reserved 4-swatch-wide footprint: PAGE_SIZE swatches at the atom's own fixed 47px width
46	 * (see `swatch.width` in zimmColourSwatch.css.ts), with no per-swatch gap
47	 * (`swatches.gap` below is 0, same as the atom's own adjacency). Two consumers share this one
48	 * value rather than each typing their own copy of the same `calc(...)` expression:
49	 *   - `swatches.width`/`minWidth`, applied only once paginated (see that part below) — keeps the
50	 *     footprint constant across a full page vs. a shorter final page.
51	 *   - `root.maxWidth`, applied unconditionally regardless of pagination (see that part below) —
52	 *     caps the whole component so `labelName`'s truncation CSS always has a definite width to
53	 *     truncate against.
54	 */
55	const GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH = `calc(${PAGE_SIZE} * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`;
56	
57	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
58	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
59	
60	  baseStyle: ({ isPaginated }: { isPaginated?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
61	    root: {
62	      display: 'flex',
63	      flexDirection: 'column',
64	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
65	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
66	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
67	      // Unconditional cap, regardless of `isPaginated` — this is a bug fix, not a stylistic
68	      // choice. `root` otherwise has no width of its own (deliberate — see the `swatches` part
69	      // below for why a short, non-paginated row must still size naturally to its actual content)
70	      // so it has no ceiling for `labelName`'s truncation CSS to truncate against: confirmed via
71	      // real Chromium rendering that a long enough colour name simply grows `root` (and the
72	      // flex-grown `labelName` span inside it) past this footprint with no ellipsis, unless some
73	      // ancestor happens to impose a definite width of its own. Capping `root` itself to the same
74	      // reserved footprint `swatches` already reserves once paginated makes truncation
75	      // self-contained in every context, rather than depending on whatever the eventual PDP page
76	      // does or doesn't constrain. `maxWidth`, not `width`: `root` must still be free to render
77	      // narrower than this when content is short (e.g. one or two short colour names) — this only
78	      // ever stops it from growing past the cap. Does not change the swatches row's own sizing
79	      // behaviour (still `100%` when non-paginated, see below) — it only changes what that `100%`
80	      // now resolves against.
81	      maxWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH,
82	    },
83	
84	    label: {
85	      display: 'flex',
86	      alignItems: 'center',
87	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
88	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
89	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
90	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
91	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
92	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
93	    },
94	
95	    labelName: {
96	      textStyle: 'caption',
97	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
98	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
99	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
100	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
101	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
102	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
103	      flex: '1 0 0',
104	      minWidth: 0,
105	      overflow: 'hidden',
106	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
107	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
108	    },
109	
110	    swatches: {
111	      display: 'flex',
112	      // Required so that off-page swatches (position:absolute, see index.tsx) are contained
113	      // within this element rather than escaping to the nearest positioned ancestor.
114	      position: 'relative',
115	      // Non-paginated (<= SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours): sizes naturally to however many
116	      // swatches are actually present. Unchanged, deliberately out of scope for this fix — there
117	      // is no confirmed design value either way for a 2- or 3-colour row's width, so nothing was
118	      // invented here.
119	      //
120	      // Paginated (> SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours, windowed to a fixed PAGE_SIZE-wide
121	      // slice per page): a plain `100%` here resolves against `root`'s own width — but `root` has
122	      // no explicit width of its own, so it auto-fits to its widest child, which is this very
123	      // element. That circular relationship meant the *rendered* width tracked how many items the
124	      // current window actually held (192px for a full 4-item page, 96px for a 2-item final
125	      // page), so `root` — and `label` above it, itself 100% of that same `root` — visibly
126	      // resized between pages. Confirmed directly in a running Storybook: the pagination chevrons
127	      // jumped position between the two pages of the `Paginated` story. Reserving
128	      // GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH regardless of the current page's real item count breaks that
129	      // loop — the footprint stays constant across every page, full or partial. A partial final
130	      // page's unused space simply remains empty to the right: the flex default
131	      // `justify-content: flex-start` already left-aligns the rendered items, so nothing further
132	      // is needed for that.
133	      width: isPaginated ? GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH : '100%',
134	      ...(isPaginated ? { minWidth: GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH } : {}),
135	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
136	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
137	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
138	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
139	      gap: 0,
140	    },
141	
142	    pagination: {
143	      display: 'flex',
144	      alignItems: 'center',
145	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
146	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
147	      // confirms a real value.
148	    },
149	
150	    pageButton: {
151	      display: 'flex',
152	      alignItems: 'center',
153	      justifyContent: 'center',
154	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
155	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
156	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls
157	      // for, with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it by the flex alignment above.
158	      padding: 0,
159	      border: 'none',
160	      background: 'none',
161	      cursor: 'pointer',
162	      // No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control — same "leave an
163	      // unspecified visual state alone rather than invent one" precedent as swatch-group's own
164	      // disabled colour logic (see this codebase's Known Gaps notes). The native `disabled`
165	      // attribute (set in index.tsx) already makes the control genuinely inert and announces as
166	      // disabled to assistive tech; only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX
167	      // keyword, not a design token.
168	      _disabled: {
169	        cursor: 'not-allowed',
170	        color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)',
171	      },
172	      // Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (zimmColourSwatch,
173	      // zimmNavItem) — --zimm-focus-ring already composites the border-width/colour pair.
174	      _focusVisible: {
175	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
176	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
177	      },
178	    },
179	  }),
180	};
